question: True or false: an able pupil who moves to a highly selective school tends to rate their own ability lower?
answer: True. Marsh and Hau tested the big-fish-little-pond effect in 26 countries: for pupils of equal ability, those among abler classmates had a lower opinion of their own academic skill. Self-image is set by the room, not by any national scale. A top pupil in an ordinary school can become an average one overnight.
move: A self-judgement is only as fair as the group you measure against.
ask: Whom am I comparing myself with, and is that the fairest group to measure against?
trap: Expecting a prestigious school to boost pupils' confidence along with results.
reference: Marsh & Hau, Big-fish-little-pond effect on academic self-concept: a cross-cultural (26-country) test of the negative effects of academically selective schools, American Psychologist, 2003
